title: PSQE: A Theoretical-Practical Approach to Pseudo Seed Quality Enhancement for Unsupervised Multimodal Entity Alignment

problem.claim: Multimodal entity alignment seeks to identify equivalent entities across modalities to support structural data integration and downstream large language model applications.

gap.claim: Unsupervised multimodal entity alignment remains underexplored because multimodal information can create imbalanced pseudo-seed coverage across the knowledge graph.

contributions.claim: PSQE enhances pseudo-seed precision and balances graph coverage using multimodal information and clustering-resampling.
The paper analyzes how pseudo-seeds affect existing contrastive-learning-based multimodal entity alignment models.
PSQE is presented as a plug-and-play module for improving baseline models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experimental results validate their theoretical findings.
The authors report that PSQE improves baseline performance by considerable margins.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal entity alignment supports cross-modal entity identification, structural data integration, and large language model applications.
Methods moved toward unsupervised alignment with pseudo-seeds to avoid difficult-to-obtain labeled seed pairs.
Multimodal unsupervised alignment remains underexplored because pseudo-seed coverage can become imbalanced across the knowledge graph.
PSQE addresses pseudo-seed precision and graph-coverage balance through multimodal information and clustering-resampling.
The paper explains pseudo-seed effects in contrastive learning and reports experiments supporting the analysis and improving baseline performance.

source_observation.claim: Imbalanced pseudo-seed coverage can cause models to prioritize high-density graph regions and weaken learning for sparse regions.

interpretation.claim: Pseudo-label quality should be evaluated jointly with its distribution across the data structure, not only by aggregate precision.

application.claim: When designing pseudo-labeling pipelines, monitor coverage balance and use resampling or related controls to prevent concentration in dense regions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that coverage balancing is beneficial for tasks or datasets beyond the reported multimodal entity-alignment setting.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and numerical improvement magnitudes are unspecified.
The theoretical assumptions, derivations, and scope of the contrastive-learning analysis are unspecified.
The effects of individual PSQE components and its computational cost are unspecified.
